 GAIGE HERRERA DEFEATS MATT SMITH AT NHRA POMONA FINALS TO COMPLETE TWO-WIN WEEKEND
 November 16, 2026 
 by 
 Bobby Bennett 
 Gaige Herrera had already beaten his teammate for one Wally on Saturday. On Sunday, he took another one from six-time world champion Matt Smith, finishing the NHRA season with two victories in two days at Pomona.   Herrera ran 6.683 seconds at 202.39 mph aboard his RevZilla/Motul/Vance & Hines Suzuki to defeat Smith in the Pro Stock Motorcycle final of the In-N-Out Burger NHRA Finals. It was his fifth victory of 2026 and the 33rd of his professional career.   “Today turned into something unbelievable,” Herrera said. “I might as well retire at this point. I don’t know if I could top that.”   The weekend began with Herrera defeating Richard Gadson in Saturday’s completion of the postponed Las Vegas final, which had been delayed by excessive wind two weeks earlier. He returned Sunday as the No. 1 qualifier and eliminated Alex Laughlin, John Hall and Ryan Oehler to earn his place opposite Smith.   Smith had beaten Marc Ingwersen and Joey Gladstone before knocking out Gadson in the semifinals, giving him his fifth final-round appearance of the season. His victory over Gadson also opened the door for Herrera to clinch his third championship by defeating Oehler.   Herrera got the better of the starting line and never surrendered the advantage. Smith had already taken care of one Vance & Hines Suzuki, but he couldn’t get past the other when the Pomona trophy was on the line.   For all the success Herrera enjoyed over the weekend, he admitted Sunday morning wasn’t particularly comfortable. Even with the quickest motorcycle in qualifying, he knew there were still four rounds between him and another national event victory.   “I woke up this morning and my stomach was turning,” Herrera said. “It was just one of those days. It’s like you want to get it over with, but you want it to go good and you don’t know what’s going to happen.”   
 Herrera generally prefers running last when he has lane choice, although Sunday’s semifinal round gave him reason to reconsider that preference. Watching the competition can be useful until somebody else’s result changes what is riding on your next pass.   “I always like going last,” Herrera said. “It’s like a double-edged sword. You get to see everyone run, but then there’s scenarios like that, then they’re in your mind when you’re in a burnout box that, ‘I got to capitalize on this and do my job.'”   The Vance & Hines team had changed engines on Gadson’s motorcycle before his semifinal meeting with Smith. Herrera believed his teammate would advance, setting up the head-to-head final he had wanted.   “We had to change motors on Richard’s bike before the semis, and I really thought he was going to perform and beat Matt,” Herrera said. “That’s ultimately what I wanted.”   Instead, Herrera found Smith waiting for him in the final, with the championship already decided. There were no points scenarios left to calculate, only another opportunity to beat one of the toughest competitors in Pro Stock Motorcycle.   Herrera credited Andrew Hines, Jay and the Vance & Hines shop personnel for preparing his Suzuki throughout the weekend. Their association began with a conversation in Las Vegas when Hines asked Herrera whether he could stay an extra day to test a motorcycle.   “When Andrew in Vegas, he tapped me on the shoulder, he’s like, ‘Are you going to be here Monday to test ride my bike?'” Herrera said. “I said, ‘I can be.’ That was the best decision I ever made.”   Pomona wasn’t unfamiliar territory when Herrera joined the professional tour. He had watched his father race there and later competed in bracket racing himself, years before he found himself lining up against Smith with another national event victory at stake.   There was no shortage of reasons for Herrera to celebrate when Sunday’s racing ended. He had beaten two world champions in separate finals over the weekend, and the second victory came at a track where he had spent years watching other racers collect trophies.   “So, very good day for me,” Herrera said. “And yeah, this is an all-time high for me.” 
 Bobby Bennett 
 Bobby Bennett is the founder, publisher and editor of CompetitionPlus.com. A Spartanburg, S.C., native, he borrowed $1,500 to launch Competition Plus as a print magazine in the late 1980s. He later worked with Super Stock & Drag Illustrated and Petersen’s Drag Racing before launching CompetitionPlus.com in 1999, driven by a vision of bringing legitimate drag racing journalism to the internet. One of the sport’s earliest dedicated online news outlets, CompetitionPlus.com grew into a daily source for breaking news, features and commentary. Bennett has covered NHRA professional and sportsman racing for more than 40 years.
